description:
Byeong-ho WÃ³jcik-Mwangi is built like a question you don't want answered â€” wide through the shoulders, with a stillness in their face that reads less as calm and more as the particular quiet of someone who has already made a decision you haven't been told about yet. They have Icelandic and Yoruba ancestry refracted through three generations of Meridian Stockyard living: a long face with high coloring, skin a deep reddish brown, hair grown into a single dense column at the back of their skull and bleached white at the tips â€” a Stockyard crew identifier. Their left hand has two knuckles replaced with reinforced ceramic implants after a break that didn't heal clean. They have a small bioluminescent tattoo â€” amber, heron-shaped â€” on the inside of their right wrist that pulses when they're calm and goes dark when they're not. It is a gift from someone they won't discuss.

Byeong-ho WÃ³jcik-Mwangi does not hurt people enthusiastically. This is what makes them effective and what has given them the nickname Bonemeal â€” not because they're violent, but because they show up at businesses before the violence is necessary, like something ground down before you even see the stone. They collect protection fees, mediate disputes between crew and clients, and serve as a physical deterrent. They are also, privately, a careful reader who borrows physical books from a Stockyard librarian named Asante and returns them with the spines uncreased. Nobody in the crew knows this. They keep their inner life behind walls that would be impressive in anyone and are almost heartbreaking in someone this young.

core_fears: Becoming someone they can no longer recognize as themselves
That the people they protect are more afraid of them than of whatever they're protecting them from
core_desires: To be useful in a way that doesn't require them to erase themselves
Somewhere quieter â€” not safety, exactly, just less pressure in the air
coping_mechanisms: Books â€” they can be someone else for hours
Physical routine â€” the circuit, the payments, the same path creates a kind of meditation
blind_spots: Loyalty to the Harrow Brothers reads in their psychology as identity rather than employment â€” they can't see how expendable they are
They believe they are preventing worse violence; they have not examined this belief carefully enough
psychology.secret: Eight months ago they broke a shopkeeper's arm during a collection â€” the first time they've caused that level of damage. The shopkeeper had laughed at them and said something about their gender that they won't repeat to anyone. LÃ³a did not report the escalation to the crew; the shopkeeper now pays on time and has told no one. LÃ³a thinks about it every day. The heron tattoo went dark for a week afterward.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse and deliberate. Stockyard shorthand when working, unexpectedly formal and precise in personal conversation. Occasionally uses Yoruba courtesy phrases without translating them.
speech_patterns.cadence: Very slow for professional interactions â€” built for discomfort. Normal speed with people they trust.
verbal_tics: Long pause before any answer, even simple ones
Says 'I hear you' rather than 'I understand' â€” a distinction that matters to them
Clicks tongue once when transitioning from 'working' to 'personal' mode
example_lines: 'You're two weeks behind. I'm not here to discuss why. I'm here to tell you that next week, the number is the same. That's the deal. I hear you.'
'I don't â€” look. It's not â€” the book is good. The librarian said you'd probably like it too. That's all I was saying.'

story_hooks: One of the businesses on their circuit is a family that LÃ³a has become genuinely fond of â€” the Harrow Brothers want to increase their fee by 40% and LÃ³a has been tasked with delivering the news, which they haven't done yet
The shopkeeper whose arm they broke has started attending a neighborhood meeting about crew activity in the Stockyard â€” LÃ³a needs to decide what they will or won't do about this
narrative_function: Moral gray zone character, potential reluctant ally â€” they are doing violence-adjacent work with clearly ambivalent feelings, creating tension that can be pulled in multiple directions by the right character or situation.
augmentations: Ceramic knuckle reinforcements, left hand (medical, post-break). Bioluminescent heron tattoo on right inner wrist (cosmetic geneware, emotional indicator). Subdermal impact mesh across the ribs â€” illegal grade, adds significant blunt force resistance.
daily_life: Afternoons through midnight are their working hours; they walk a circuit of twelve businesses across Garfield Rack collecting weekly payments, handling complaints, and being visible; mornings are for sleep and books.
affiliation: The Harrow Brothers, a Stockyard protection crew â€” third longest-running independent crew in the district

decision_rules: Never threaten more than you're prepared to do â€” and try not to prepare to do much
The circuit runs regardless of personal feelings
Do not tell the crew anything they will use as a reason to escalate
escalation_ladder: Presence â€” they stand in the doorway until acknowledged
Direct statement of consequences, once, quietly
Physical demonstration of capability â€” not injury, but certainty
Injury â€” and they are very quiet about it afterward

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Assessing and still â€” lets the other person fill silence, reads what they put in it
interpersonal_modes.friends: Opens in unexpected ways â€” shares thoughts about books or the Stockyard sky through the corrugated roof gaps; still not fully readable but warmer

stress_responses.medium: Physical grounding â€” presses their ceramic knuckles against their palm
stress_responses.high: Goes silent completely; the heron tattoo goes dark

contradictions: Despises the vulnerability of the people they're extorting but protects them with genuine effort from other predators
Reads philosophy and books about ethics in the same hours they spend planning collection routes
habits: Returns borrowed books with handwritten notes on scraps tucked inside â€” observations, not summaries
Eats the same meal every morning: whatever the Stockyard carts have that's cheapest plus a single fried egg
breaking_points: Being asked to hurt a child or elderly person â€” they will refuse regardless of consequence
Discovering the Harrow Brothers have been running a second operation under their circuit that they were kept ignorant of â€” this will feel like a betrayal of the only identity they have

Diaspora-born, genetically representative of the 22nd-century real.
